question:
What is the value of

\[ \sum_{n=2}^{255} \frac{\log_2\left(1 + \frac{1}{n}\right)}{(\log_2 n)(\log_2(n+1))}? \]
solution:
The logarithm in the numerator is a difference of the two logarithms in the denominator, which lets us split each summand into terms that cancel.

The quotient rule for logarithms gives
\[
\log_2\left(1+\frac1n\right)
=\log_2\left(\frac{n+1}{n}\right)
=\log_2(n+1)-\log_2 n.
\]
Since \(n\ge2\), both denominator logarithms are positive. Therefore,
\[
\frac{\log_2(n+1)-\log_2 n}{(\log_2 n)(\log_2(n+1))}
=\frac1{\log_2 n}-\frac1{\log_2(n+1)}.
\]
The sum becomes
\[
\left(\frac1{\log_2 2}-\frac1{\log_2 3}\right)
+\left(\frac1{\log_2 3}-\frac1{\log_2 4}\right)
+\cdots+
\left(\frac1{\log_2 255}-\frac1{\log_2 256}\right).
\]
Every interior term cancels. Because \(256=2^8\), the result is
\[
\frac1{\log_2 2}-\frac1{\log_2 256}
=1-\frac18=\boxed{\frac78},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
